package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions distributed via Google Play Store and 9Apps during campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because it disguises itself as a legitimate app, then exploits Android vulnerabilities to modify pre-installed applications, injecting code to display fraudulent ads and generate illicit revenue. This behavior subverts user trust, abuses device permissions, and monetizes through unauthorized ad fraud.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into pre-installed application code (APK files) after initial installation

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the code scans for vulnerable pre-installed apps, injects malicious ad-displaying code into their APKs, and reinstalls the modified apps, resulting in fraudulent ad display at runtime.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying other installed applications to inject code is highly abnormal and a strong indicator of malware. Legitimate apps do not patch or replace other apps' APKs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps do not alter or repackage other installed applications. This behavior violates app sandboxing and user trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System update tools or device management software (with explicit user consent and system-level privileges) may update or patch apps, but not inject adware.
key_indicators: Scans for and modifies other installed apps
Reinstalls patched APKs without user consent

execution_context.file_location: Injected ad module within patched APKs

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code fetches ad content from a remote server and displays fraudulent ads as overlays within the compromised app, generating revenue for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Displaying ads via injected code in unrelated apps is a hallmark of adware and fraudulent monetization. The code operates without user consent and outside the original app's intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps display ads only within their own context and with user awareness. Injecting ads into other apps is deceptive.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Ad SDKs in legitimate apps display ads, but only within the app's own UI and with user consent.
key_indicators: Fetches ad content from attacker-controlled server
Displays overlay ads in unrelated apps

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly innocent app from Google Play Store or 9Apps.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of malicious payload

attack_chain.action: Malware scans device for vulnerable pre-installed apps and injects malicious ad code into their APKs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Patched apps with embedded adware are installed

attack_chain.action: Patched apps, when launched, execute injected code to fetch and display fraudulent ads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous ad fraud and revenue generation for attacker

behavioral_signatures: App modifies or replaces other installed APKs
Injected code in unrelated apps displays ads or overlays
Unexpected network requests from system or pre-installed apps
file_indicators: APK files with unexpected code sections or ad modules
Presence of adware modules in non-ad apps
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known ad fraud or attacker-controlled domains
Frequent ad content fetches from non-standard ad networks
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that attempt to modify or reinstall other APKs, especially those that inject ad modules into unrelated apps. Analyze network traffic for unexpected ad content requests from system or pre-installed apps. Use file integrity checks to detect repackaged APKs and scan for known adware code signatures within app packages.
